references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 23:29-30|Matthew 23:29-30] contains the same rebuke against the scribes and Pharisees who build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the graves of the righteous, while they themselves are sons of those who killed the prophets.

In [ref:2 Krøn 24:20-21|2 Chronicles 24:20-21], the prophet Zechariah, son of Jehoiada, is stoned to death in the temple courtyard – an example of how the fathers killed the prophets, as Jesus accuses them.
In [ref:1 Kong 18:4|1 Kings 18:4], it is told that Jezebel killed the Lord's prophets, and Obadiah hid a hundred prophets in caves. This shows how Israel's fathers persecuted and killed the prophets.

In [ref:1 Kong 19:10|1 Kings 19:10], Elijah complains that the people of Israel have abandoned the Lord's covenant, torn down his altars, and killed his prophets with the sword – an example of the fathers' persecution of the prophets.

In [ref:Jer 2:30|Jeremiah 2:30], the Lord says that the people of Israel struck their own prophets to death, "like a destroying lion." This is the background for Jesus' words about how the fathers killed the prophets.
In [ref:Apg 7:52|Acts 7:52], Stephen asks the same question: "Which of the prophets have your fathers not persecuted?" – a direct parallel to Jesus' accusation in this verse.

In [ref:1 Tess 2:15|1 Thessalonians 2:15], Paul writes about the Jews who killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and who persecuted the apostles – an echo of Jesus' words about the fathers who killed the prophets.
